full_judgment:
Rule in CR No. 10039 of 1991 at the instance of petitioner Md. Ashabullah is against judgment and order dated 31.8.1987 passed by Subordinate Judge, Habiganj in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 10 of 1981 dismissing the appeal and affirming judgment and order dated 29.11.80 passed by Munsif Habiganj in Miscellaneous Case No. 146 of 1973 under section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Opposite party No. 1 Renu Pada Chakraborty of this Rule is petitioner in the other Civil Revision No. 9371 of 1991 and opposite party No. 1 of that Rule is the petitioner of CR No. 10039 of 1991 and, as such, both the Rules are substantially between the same parties and over the self same property and, as such, both these Rules are disposed of by this judgment. 

 3. The suit was contested by defendant No. 1 denying material allegations and stating that Kunja Mohan Chakraborty was a childless person and defendant No. 1 and his father used to serve said Kunja Mohan Chakraborty in various ways-and in consideration of their services Kunja Mohan Chakraborty settled suit land to the defendant No. 1 and his father allowing them to possess the same without rent for 20 years after developing the same and to pay rent of Taka one and one anna after expiry of 20 years and executed a hukumnama or permission deed in their favour embodying the said terms and since then they are in possession of the suit land by producing paddy after making substantial improvement of the suit land by cutting earth from the bank of the dighi and filling the dighi at huge cost and labour. His further case is, that title and possession of Kunja Mohan Chakraborty was extinguished in the suit property from the date of settlement of the same with defendant No. 1 and his father since Magh, 1359 BS and they have been in continuous possession of the same by producing paddy and filed Miscellaneous Case No. 146 of 1973 for correction of SA khatian as the same was wrongly recorded in the name of said Kunja Mohan Chakraborty and he has been paying rent with the Tahsil Office. His further case is, that taking advantage of his poverty as some powerful men of the locality with the help of the plaintiff attempted to dispossess him from the suit land he filed Title Suit No. 148 of 1974 in which plaintiff admitted his possession by filing written statement and he got decree in that suit on 27.11.76 for perpetual injunction and thereafter plaintiff filed a criminal case against him under sections 379 and 427 of the Penal Code on the allegation of cutting paddy and the said case was dismissed on 17.5.75 and the plaintiff has or had no title and possession in the suit land and he filed the suit with false allegations. 

 6. Court of appeal below concurred with the trial Court as to plaintiffs acquisition of title in the properties left by Kunja Mohan Chakraborty on the basis of probated will in favour of the plaintiff. But the Court of appeal below on consideration of evidence of PWs and DWs, as well as decree in Title Suit No. 148 of 1974 for perpetual injunction passed on 27.11.76 in favour of the defendant No. 1 and against the plaintiff and also on consideration of criminal Court's order dated 12.9.74 and 27.11.74 passed in paddy theft case and also in a proceeding under section 144 CrPC came to the conclusion that plaintiff failed to prove his case of possession and dispossession from the suit land. Court of appeal below further considered the document Ext. 'Ka' executed by Kunja Mohan Chakraborty on 19.2.53 in favour of defendant No. 1 and also his evidence as DW 1 that he filled up the dighi in the suit land and made the same cultivable and there is no existence of cremation ground since Magh, 1359 BS and he has been possessing the same by cultivating paddy and he did not dispossess the plaintiff against whom he got decree for perpetual injunction. Court of appeal below further considered the evidence of DW Nos. 2-5 who corroborated evidence of DW 1, Court of appeal below further considered the evidence of Advocate Commissioner DW 6 Aminul Islam who held local inspection of the suit land on 10.8.85 and did not find existence of any cremation ground in the suit land. Relying upon the same, Court of appeal below came to the conclusion that the defendant is in possession of the suit land from before the alleged date of dispossession and hence dismissed the suit and allowed the appeal and set aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court. 

 7. It appears that defendant filed and proved his unregistered document written and executed in a plain sheet of paper by Kunja Mohan Chakraborty in favour of defendant No. 1 and his father Ext 'Ka', By this document Kunja Mohan Chakraborty permitted defendant No. 1 and his father to possess the suit land which is dighi and its bank for 20 years without any rent in consideration of service rendered by them to him by making the same fit for cultivation at their own cost and labour and thereafter to possess the same on payment of annual rent of Taka 1 and one Anna to him becoming absolute owner of the suit property in tenancy right, SA Khatian Ext. 'Kha' recorded the suit land in the name of Kunja Mohan Chakraborty but in column 23 thereof suit plot No. 199 having an area of 52 decimals has been shown in permissive possession of defendant No. 1 and his father Abdul Hakim and suit plot No. 201 having an area of 6 decimals has been shown as cremation ground for the use of members of the Hindu community. 2 rent receipts Ext. Kha(1) and Kha (2) show that Abdul Hakim paid rent of the suit land for some years. Aforesaid Hukumnama Ext. 'Ka' and SA Khatian Ext. 'Kha' were considered by the Court in Title Suit No. 148 of 1974 to find possession in favour of the plaintiff of that suit i.e. defendant No. 1 of the present suit between the plaintiff and defendant No. 1. Finding of possession in that suit is binding upon the plaintiff. There is no non-reading and misreading of the evidence on record on the part of the Court of appeal below in setting aside the finding of possession by the trial Court. I, therefore, find no reason to interfere with the said finding of possession in the impugned judgment. 

 8. Pertinent question in this Rule is whether plaintiff petitioner is entitled to recover possession of the suit land from the defendants as legatee under the will executed by Kunja Mohan Chakraborty and probated by him. Court of appeal below found that the defendants are in possession of the suit land cutting the bank and filling the dighi at their cost and labour and there is no existence of cremation ground in the suit land and the defendants are in possession from before the alleged date of dispossession. Since the defendant No.1 and his late father possessed the suit land after making substantial improvements being authorised under the said hukumnama or permission deed Ext 'Ka', Kunja Mohan Chakraborty, executant of the said deed, could not evict the defendants as he would have been bound by his promise made in the said deed. Due to intervention of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1951 defendant No. 1 could not acquire tenancy right under the said Kunja Mohan Chakraborty or his legatee since long before completion of 20 years all rent receiving interests were acquired and right of any owner of any land to create tenancy in favour of anyone was taken away. Under the said Ext. 'Ka' permissive possession of defendant No. 1 and his late father in the suit property would have ended on 19.2.73 and their tenancy right would have commenced from 20.2.73 had State Acquisition and Tenancy Act not intervened in the meantime. In the absence of creation of tenancy right continuance of defendants in possession of the suit land from 20.2.73 can only be adverse to the owner of the land. Plaintiff having filed the suit on 29.9.83 i.e. within 12 years from that date normally he could have recovered possession of the suit land on the basis of his title. But under the equitable principle of promissory estoppel Kunja Mohan Chakraborty and after his death plaintiff petitioner as his legatee is debarred from recovering possession from the defendants as they made substantial improvement of the suit land at their own cost and labour relying upon the assurance made by the previous owner Kunja Mohan Chakraborty. Equitable principles are the tools for mitigating the rigours of law. In this case equitable principle of estoppel as embodied in the Evidence Act debars the plaintiff petitioner from recovering possession from the defendant opposite parties though they did not acquire 'title in the suit land by adverse possession on the date of filing the suit. I, therefore, find nothing illegal in the impugned judgment in allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree of the trial Court. The Rule in Civil Revision No. 9371 of 1991 is therefore, discharged with cost. 

 9. As to the Rule is Civil Revision No. 10039 of 1991 at the instance of Md. Ashabullah against judgment of affirmance in view of the fact already noticed in the other Rule that suit plot No. 199 was recorded in the permissive possession of the petitioner of this Rule during the SA operation when he did not acquire any tenancy right in the suit property, learned Advocate for the petitioner does not seriously press this Rule. I also do not find any illegality in the impugned judgment to interfere with the same inasmuch as concerned SA Khatian correctly recorded the .state of the land existing at the time of the SA survey operation. But that will not debar the petitioner of this Rule from mutating his name is the concerned SA Khatian on the basis of the appellate decree in his favour affirmed in the other Rule being Civil Revision No. 9371 of 1991.
